questions.question: A growing country is one with ________ .
questions.solution:
A growing country is one with __**rising GNP at constant prices.**__

 
• GNP stands for - Gross national product.
 
• It is the market value of all the services and goods produced per year by property and labor provided by the residents of a country- both within the geographical boundaries and outside.
 
• GNP = Money value of everything produced within the country + Incoming money from outside - Outgoing money to abroad

Or simply put it,

Here, GDP stands for Gross Domestic Product, which is the money value of products and services produced within the country during a specified period of time.

questions.question: The per capita income in India was Rs. 20 in 1867-68, was ascertained for the first time by________.
questions.solution:
The per capita income in India was Rs. 20 in 1867-68, was ascertained for the first time by DadabhaiNaoroji.

 
• The average income earned per person in a particular area in a specific year is called as Per Capita Income.
 
• It is found by dividing the total income of an area by its total population.

questions.solution:

questions.question: In which month does the Earth's Perihelion position occur?
questions.solution:
The Earth's Perihelion position occurs in the month of **January**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

__
 
• Perihelion is a point in the orbit of a planet at which the planet is closest to the sun. Around **3rd January**__, the earth is nearest to the sun.
 
• During the earth’s revolution around the sun, the earth is farthest from the sun around 4th July. This position of the earth is called aphelion. ​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The solar output received at the top of the atmosphere varies slightly in a year due to the variations in the distance between the earth and the sun.
 
• During its revolution around the sun, the earth is farthest from the sun on July 4. (Aphelion)
 
• During Aphelion earth will be 152 million km away from the sun.
 
• On January 3, the earth is nearest to the sun (147 million km) and this position is called Perihelion.
 
• The annual insolation received by the earth on January 3 is slightly more than the amount received on July 4.
 
• Since the effect of this variation is masked by other factors like the distribution of land and sea and atmospheric circulation, this variation in the solar output does not have a great effect on daily weather changes on the surface of the earth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3ce34330a1ba061864b0aad3578e8a25958b250bfeb92ba905018be722a2d60b.png]

questions.question: The McMahon Line, which sets the boundary between India and China, is drawn to the northern boundary of which of the following states?
questions.solution:
The McMahon Line, which sets the boundary between India and China, is drawn to the northern boundary of Arunachal Pradesh.

 
• The McMahon Line is the effective borderline between the North-east region of Indiaand Tibetan region of China.
 
• It separates Arunachal Pradesh from Tibet.
 
• It was named after Sir Henry McMahon, the then foreign secretary of British India, who was also the chief negotiator at the 1914 Simla Convention.
 
• The McMahon line extends for 890 km from Bhutan in the West to 260 km east of the great bend of the Brahmaputra in the east along the crest of the Himalayas.

questions.question: Who was the Guru of the music maestro Tansen?
questions.solution:
__**Haridas**__ was the Guru of the music maestro Tansen.

• He was a great musician and the most influential personality in Hindustani Classical music.
 
• He wrote two classic books on music Sri Ganesh Stotra and Sangita Sara.

questions.question: At which place a joint military exercise named ‘SAMPRITI’ was held in November 2017 between Bangladesh and India?
questions.solution:
A joint military exercise named ‘SAMPRITI’ was held in November 2017 between Bangladesh and India at Mizoram.

 
• SAMPRITI is a bilateral defence cooperation endeavor between India and Bangladesh. 
 
• The joint military exercise had two distinct components which included Command Post Exercise (CPX) and Field Training Exercise (FTX).
 
• The CPX focused on the planning of counter-terrorist operations whereas FTX focused on company/platoon level tactical drills. 
 
• The closing ceremony was held at Counter Insurgency and Jungle Warfare School, Vairengte in Mizoram.

questions.question: Who among the following has been awarded the Arjuna award 2017 for his contribution to hockey?

questions.question: Myanmar is the _________ largest country in Southeast Asia.
questions.solution:
Myanmar is the second largest country in Southeast Asia.

 
• Myanmar (part of Mainland Southeast Asia), formerly known as Burma, is the second largest country in South-East Asia.
 
• It shares border with Bangladesh, India, China, Laos, and Thailand.
 
• Myanmar is also known as “The Golden Land” to visitors because of its glittering pagodas everywhere.

· The largest country in Southeast Asia is Indonesia (part of Maritime Southeast Asia)

 
• Southeast Asia is geographically divided into two sub-regions, known as Mainland Southeast Asia and Maritime Southeast Asia.

questions.question:
Which among the following statements are TRUE regarding synthetic fibre?

I. They melt after catching fire. 

II. They are more durable.

III. They are prepared by a number of processes using petrochemicals.
questions.solution:
All I, II and III

 
• Synthetic fibres are also called artificial fibres or man-made fibres.
 
• They are a chain of small units of chemical substances joined together. When many such single units are combined to form a single unit, it is called as Polymer.
 
• The synthetic fibre melts after catching fire and the cloth sticks to the body of the person wearing it. It is, thus, a disadvantage of synthetic fibres, e.g. Polyester clothes.
 
• They are more durable and affordable than the natural fibres, e.g. Plastic.
 
• They are synthesized from raw materials of petroleum origin, called petrochemicals.

questions.question: Which of the following products can be obtained from coal processing?
questions.solution:
Coke, Coal tar,and Coal gas can be obtained from coal processing.

 
• These products are obtained when coal is processed by heating in the absence of air.
 
• Coal gas is a mixture of hydrogen, methane and some amount of carbon dioxide and it is used as a fuel in fuel industries.
 
• Coal tar is made up about 200 carbon compounds and its products are used to make drugs, synthetic fibres, etc.
 
• Coke is 98% carbon which is mostly used as a reducing agent during extraction of metals.

questions.question: Under which Article of Indian Constitution a citizen can move to the Supreme Court of India if his Fundamental Rights are breached?
questions.solution:
Under __**Article 32**__ of the Indian Constitution, a citizen can move to the Supreme Court of India if his Fundamental Rights are breached.

 
• Right to Constitutional Remedies: Article 32 (i) of our Constitution empowers the citizens to move to the Supreme Court in case they feel they are unduly deprived of their Fundamental Rights.
 
• Dr. B R Ambedkar, the chief architect of the Constitution of India, considered “Right to Constitutional Remedies” to be the ‘heart and soul’ of the Indian Constitution.

questions.question: For how much duration members of municipalities are elected?
questions.solution:
The members of municipalities are elected for a period of Five years.

 
• 74th Amendment Act of 1992 added a new Part IX-A to the Constitution of India, entitled as ‘The Municipalities’.
 
• It consists of provisions from Article 243-P to 243-ZG.
 
• This Act provides for a five-year term of office for every municipality.
 
• All the members of the municipality are elected directly by the people of that municipal area (wards).
 
• The State Election Commission is responsible for the preparation and conduct of all elections to the municipalities.

questions.question: How many versions of each trait will be there in each child as per the rules for the inheritance of traits?
questions.solution:
__**EXPLANATION:**__

 
• Two versions of each trait will be there in each child as per the rules for the inheritance of traits.
 
• The process by which the offspring acquire traits from their parents is called Inheritance.
 
• The fundamental rules of Inheritance were given by Gregor Mendel in 1865.
 
• According to Mendel's theory, a gene could have several types, known as alleles. For example, the gene for height in pea plants would have two types, tall and short. Also, each individual would have two copies of a given gene, since one would be inherited, at random, from each parent. 
 
• His results suggested that if the two copies were of different types then in such cases only one type would be expressed biologically i.e. the effects of only one would be observed in the individual's physical characteristics, while the other would remain hidden. The former type is the dominant allele, and the latter is known as the recessive allele.

questions.question: A body of mass 3 kg accelerates from 10 m/s to 20 m/s in 5 seconds due to the application of a force on it. Calculate the magnitude of this force (in N).
questions.solution:
Acceleration = ( final velocity – initial velocity) ÷ time taken

Here, final velocity = 20 m/s and initial velocity = 10m/s and time = 5 seconds

**Therefore**, acceleration = (20 – 10) ÷ 5

= 2 m/s².

**Now**,

Force = Mass × Acceleration

Here, force = 3 × 2

 = 6 N.

questions.question: The weather reports are prepared by the __________ Department of the Government.
questions.solution:
The weather reports are prepared by the Meteorological Department of the Government.

 
• Meteorology is the study of the processes and phenomena of the atmosphere, mainly as a means of weather forecasting.

questions.question: In Microsoft Word, file, edit, view etc. are provided in ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Menu bar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

In Microsoft Word, File, edit, view etc. are provided in the Menu Bar.

Microsoft Word is a word processing package. It is used to create letters, reports, etc.

 
• Several parts of the Word window are:
 
 
• Title Bar: A topmost portion of any window
 
• Menu Bar: The bar just below the Title Bar
 
• Menu Bar options: The menu bar contains options like File, Edit, View, etc.
 
• Pull-down Menu: It is a vertical box containing a list of commands generated by each menu bar options
 
• Toolbar: It lies horizontally below the menu bar containing pictorial buttons of commands. In Microsoft Word, there are many toolbars like Standard Toolbar, Formatting Toolbar, Drawing Toolbar, Forms Toolbar, Tables and Borders Toolbar, etc.
